section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the connection between the encompassing level of Chayah and the internal levels of Nefesh, Ruach, and Neshamah is achieved through the service of self-sacrifice (mesirut nefesh) stemming from the level of Yechidah, which unifies all faculties in fulfilling G-d's will.
section.t: And likewise is it in the service of man,
that in order for there to be a connection of the aspect of Chayah
(encompassing)
with the aspect of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah
(internal),
so that the love of "with all your soul" will be felt also in the internal powers
[and likewise the connection of the intellect and the emotions],
it is through the service of mesirut nefesh (self-sacrifice),
which is from the aspect of Yechidah.
And one can explain from the elucidations on this,
that by one giving himself over to G-dliness,
the essence of all his powers is to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And since the encompassing and the internal
[and likewise the intellect and the emotions]
their essence is not their own existence but rather to fulfill the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,
therefore they do not contradict each other, and on the contrary, they become joined together.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the enactment to recite one hundred blessings daily was specifically when one hundred people died each day, because the revelation of the power of self-sacrifice comes through concealments, and the one hundred blessings unite the encompassing and filling aspects through the letter Alef of "one hundred."
section.t: And this is that the enactment to recite one hundred blessings each day was specifically when one hundred souls died each day,
because the revelation of the power of mesirut nefesh is through concealments and veils.
[And according to the known principle
that in the time of exile,
and particularly in the generation of the footsteps of Moshiach,
the power of mesirut nefesh is more revealed than in the time of the Holy Temple].
And therefore,
the enactment to recite one hundred blessings was specifically after one hundred souls died each day,
because this that each day one hundred souls died
(for one hundred souls is the completeness of number)
is because they were then in a state opposite to freedom from the Angel of Death,
which is the evil inclination,
and through this the power of their mesirut nefesh was then aroused.
And therefore they enacted then to recite one hundred blessings,
through which is made the connection of the Surrounding and the Filling,
because through the revelation
(of the power of mesirut nefesh that is from)
the Yechidah, there is a drawing down of Atik,
the Alef of "one hundred,"
the aspect of "one and not in number,"
and through this is made the connection of "Mah"
(Filling)
and "Me'ah"
(Surrounding),
read not "Mah" but "Me'ah."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the Midrash that "Now" implies repentance, and that the verse "Now Israel, what does G-d ask of you" refers to one hundred blessings, because the revelation of self-sacrifice is primarily through repentance, enabling the service of one hundred blessings.
section.t: And based on this, we can also explain the statement of the Midrash
"There is no 'Now' except the language of repentance, as it is said, 'Now Israel, what does Hashem your G-d ask of you.'"
And according to the known principle
that all the interpretations of that verse are connected to each other,
it is understood
that this that "Hashem your G-d asks of you 'Mah'"
— one hundred blessings —
is related to the matter of repentance,
and "Now."
For since penitents conquer their inclination more than the completely righteous,
and in order for a person to be able to stand against his inclination, it is through remembering the matter of mesirut nefesh,
therefore,
the primary revelation of the power of mesirut nefesh is in penitents.
And this is "Now etc., 'What does Hashem your G-d ask of you,'"
for through the revelation of mesirut nefesh that comes through repentance,
"Now,"
it is possible to have the matter of one hundred blessings,
"What does Hashem your G-d ask of you."
